verdicts.reason: All rules hold: each field is a quote with a file:line or log-line locator read back by python3 or git ls-files, covering entry file, invariant, do-not-touch list and log line; reliable matches the brief; unmatched is a valid result; and checkRunnable is false.

All rules hold: a non-zero exit on the unedited tree with expected and actual quoted from the run output is program-readable and covers the command, pinned input, actual next to expected, and red before any edit; reliable is limited to when a harness exists, harness absent is a valid result, and pytest/unittest are registered.

All rules hold: a sorted set comparison of git diff --name-only, a def/class line check and a per-hunk comment check are program-readable and cover named files, a stable signature, notes on non-obvious hunks, and a diff that matches the plan; assisted respects the brief's 'Assisted to reliable', an empty diff is valid, and checkRunnable is false.

A3 fails: the brief requires the screenshot to be compared to the fixture, but the done-when swaps in a cmp of a text file (fixture.txt) even though Bash:playwright is registered for a real screenshot check.

A3 fails: the done-when only checks that the enumerated count matches the manifest; it does not enforce one file shape per transform, an isolated copy per worker, or rejection of files whose results were not rechecked, all of which the brief names.

A3 fails: the quote-or-drop check never requires a comment to be a logic miss, security reach, or performance path, so quoted style comments pass even though the brief names those three classes and flags over-commenting.

All rules hold: the hops are file:line locators checked to contain the function name, and one hop is matched to a log line by line number read back with python3, covering entry to store, the module per hop, one log match and no tour; assisted matches the brief, log unmatched is a valid result, and checkRunnable is false.
